optimize_reason: EMEA regional-repair attempt: lengthen the cash-return-on-assets comparison from one year to two. European issuers predominantly report semi-annually, so a 252-day year-over-year difference updates too infrequently inside EMEA and the signal goes stale between filings; a 504-day baseline aligns better with the regional reporting cadence while still filtering single-period noise.

Widen the cross-sectional benchmark of the regional-best construction from sector to the whole market. Benchmarking against the entire market maximizes retained dispersion and keeps both sides of the book populated inside every region, which is the direct lever on the two failing regional Sharpes.

Intermediate benchmark granularity (industry) between the tested sector and subindustry extremes, on the construction that already gives the best EMEA reading. Maps the granularity axis completely so the remaining regional gap can be attributed either to benchmark choice or to something structural.

Pair the depreciation-free numerator (EBITDA, which removes the cross-jurisdiction depreciation-policy differences that hurt earnings measures outside AMER) with industry-level platform neutralization, on the sector benchmark. Tests whether the combination that best handles accounting heterogeneity also lifts the EMEA and APAC readings.
